title: Mont Blanc massif destablilized by summer heatwaves and rockfalls
subhead: As a result of extreme temperatures, which have weakened both its ice and its rock faces, the highest peak in the Alps is currently inaccessible by any of its three standard climbing routes.

subhead: Heat waves and the lack of rain have created particularly unfavorable conditions for tiger mosquitoes. But activity is expected to rebound in September as rainfall returns.

title: In Italy, an unusual political compromise could create a public body to support the film industry
subhead: MPs will debate a bill in September to establish an 'agency for cinema and audiovisual media' against a backdrop of budget austerity. However, the plan would still leave significant powers in the hands of political authorities.

subhead: The series inspired by 'Green Lantern,' one of the oldest superhero comics, revisits the theme of humanity’s protectors as imperfect beings.

title: In Kyiv, fleeting moments of celebration stolen from the war: 'Never in my life have I seen so many beautiful people in one place'
subhead: For the second year in a row, the Vyriy music and visual arts festival brought together several thousand people in Kyiv on August 8 and 9, despite relentless Russian drone attacks. Soldiers on leave and families joined partygoers to dance and celebrate Ukrainian folklore inside this rare bubble of peace.

Why are heatwaves becoming more frequent in France?
subhead: Between May and July, France was the most abnormally hot country in the world, compared to its average heat index. While the role of global warming is not under debate, the frequency of this summer's heatwaves is a topic of scientific debate.

title: 'The Taliban preach purity and morality, but rush to strip women in prison': A land of terror for Afghan women
subhead: 'Voices of Afghan Women' (5/6). In Afghanistan, the law now stands against women and girls. Two new decrees issued by the Taliban regime even legalize domestic violence and child marriage.

title: Why Le Pen's plan for a constitutional referendum would be 'a coup d'état in form and content'
subhead: If she were to win, far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen has pledged to call a referendum to revise the Constitution and enshrine the far right's core principles in it. According to a member of the highest administrative court, this would be 'a double coup d'état, both in form and content.'
